title: The か particle
summary: か turns a statement into a question-like idea that can sit inside another sentence: whether, or, maybe, I wonder, as if. It is always uncertain, never a confirmed fact.

blocks.text: At the end of a polite sentence **か** marks a question. In casual speech your tone of voice does that job, because a bare か at the end of a casual sentence sounds blunt and rough. But か does most of its work **inside** sentences, and every use grows from one idea: **it turns a statement into something uncertain, like a question**.
Put か after a clause and the clause becomes a noun-like "whether ...". It can then be the object of words like 分からない (do not know) or 知っている (know). You normally add no が or を after か.

blocks.jp: さくらが来るか分からない。
blocks.en: I do not know whether Sakura will come.

blocks.jp: これは誰の本か分かりますか。
blocks.en: Do you know whose book this is?

blocks.text: The whole question sits in one carriage. The engine 分からない is about that carriage.
**かどうか** spells out "or not" and makes the uncertainty explicit.

blocks.jp: 来るかどうか分からない。
blocks.en: I do not know whether (she) will come or not.

blocks.text: "Or" always means uncertain: it might be A, it might be B. That is why か fits between two nouns.

blocks.jp: お茶かコーヒー、どっちがいい？
blocks.en: Tea or coffee, which do you want?

blocks.text: It is built from three pieces. か gives "whether she comes", も adds "even", and 知れない means "cannot be known". Put together: "even whether she comes cannot be known", so "she might come".

blocks.jp: 田中さんは来るかもしれない。

blocks.text: か plus the soft ending な, which is how we talk to ourselves. The result is "I wonder ...".

blocks.en: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

blocks.text: ものか / もんか: as if!
もの is a "thing", so this asks "is that a thing?" and expects the answer "of course not". It is a question used to deny, like English "Would I do that?". It sounds rough and emphatic.

blocks.jp: そんな物を食べるもんか。
blocks.en: As if I would eat such a thing!

blocks.text: ところ is a "point", so どころか says "not even at this point", and then names something even smaller or nearer.

blocks.jp: 漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない。
blocks.en: Far from kanji, I cannot even read hiragana.

rows: か + も + しれない
blocks.title: Set phrases made of か

blocks.text: As in lesson 26, か marks a situation as imagined, not real: ゆうれいを見た**か**のような顔, "a face as if she had seen a ghost".

items: **Clause + か + 分からない / 知らない**: whether ...
**か + どうか**: whether or not.
**A か B**: A or B; **かもしれない**: might; **かな**: I wonder.
**ものか / もんか**: strong rhetorical denial.

questions.prompt: あした雨が降るか、知っていますか。
questions.note: A buried question.
questions.en: Do you know whether it will rain tomorrow?

questions.instruction: What does かどうか add?
questions.prompt: このカレーが辛いかどうか、聞いてみた。
questions.note: かどうか: whether or not.
questions.en: I asked whether this curry is spicy or not.

questions.prompt: 駅はどこ＿＿教えてください。
questions.note: A buried question uses か.
questions.en: Please tell me where the station is.

questions.prompt: テストが難しい＿＿どうか、まだ分かりません。
questions.note: か + どうか: whether or not.
questions.en: I do not know yet whether the test is hard or not.

questions.prompt: コーヒー＿＿お茶、どちらがいいですか。
questions.note: A か B: A or B.
questions.en: Coffee or tea, which would you like?

questions.prompt: 田中さんは、もう帰ったかもしれない。
options: Mr. Tanaka may have already gone home
Mr. Tanaka must have gone home
Mr. Tanaka has not gone home
questions.note: か + も + しれない: might.
questions.en: Mr. Tanaka may have already gone home.

options: "I wonder if it will be sunny"
questions.note: か + な: said to oneself.
questions.en: I wonder if it will be sunny tomorrow.

questions.prompt: あんな高い車、買うものか。
options: As if I would buy such an expensive car!
questions.note: ものか: a rhetorical denial.
questions.en: As if I would buy such an expensive car!

questions.instruction: What does どころか do?
questions.prompt: お金どころか、時間もない。
options: Far from X, not even Y
questions.note: どころか: far from the nearer thing.
questions.en: Far from money, I do not even have time.

questions.instruction: What does かのよう suggest?
questions.prompt: まるで雪が降っているかのようだ。
options: An imagined situation, not a real one
questions.note: か marks the situation as pretend.
questions.en: It is as if snow were falling.

questions.instruction: Does か here state a fact?
questions.prompt: 雨が降るかもしれない。
questions.note: か keeps things uncertain.
questions.en: It might rain.

options: 誰が来るか知りません。
誰が来るを知りません。
questions.note: After a buried question use か, not を.

questions.instruction: What does A か B mean?
questions.note: か between nouns: or.
questions.en: Apples or mandarins.

questions.note: かな: wondering to oneself.
questions.en: I wonder what time it is.

questions.prompt: どこへ行くか決めましたか。
options: Have you decided where to go?
questions.note: か buries the question "where to go".
questions.en: Have you decided where to go?

questions.prompt: I don't know what he ate.
questions.note: Clause + か + 分かりません.
questions.en: I don't know what he ate.

questions.prompt: I wonder if Mom is home.
questions.note: Clause + かな.
questions.en: I wonder if Mom is home.

questions.prompt: Please tell me if you can come or not.
questions.note: か + どうか.
questions.en: Please tell me if you can come or not.

questions.note: か + も + しれない.
questions.en: He might be sick.

questions.prompt: Far from tea, we do not even have water.
questions.note: どころか: far from.
questions.en: Far from tea, we do not even have water.

questions.instruction: Tap the clause that became "when" (a buried question)
questions.note: Clause + か.
questions.en: I do not know when it will end.

questions.note: か + も + しれない.
questions.en: That person might be a student.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that denies strongly
questions.note: ものか: a rhetorical denial.
questions.en: As if I would listen to such a story!
